solution.text: <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal"></mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> are not equally stable. Li atom is much larger in size than H-atom. The bond order in <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is much larger than bond length in <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub><mo>.</mo></math> Moreover, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> molecule has two electrons in the antibonding molecular orbital while <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> has no electrons in the antiobinding molecular orbital. Thus, <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is less sable than <math display="block"> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>H</mtext> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <mtext>(Bond</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>energy</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>of</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msub> <mrow> <mtext>Li</mtext></mrow> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <mtext> </mtext><mtext>=</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>110</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>kJ</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msup> <mrow> <mtext>mol</mtext></mrow> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mtext>2</mtext></mrow> </msup> <mtext> </mtext><mtext>+</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>Bond</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>energy</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>of</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msub> <mtext>H</mtext> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <mtext> </mtext><mtext>=</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>438</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>kJ</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msup> <mrow> <mtext>mol</mtext></mrow> <mrow> <mo>−</mo><mtext>1</mtext></mrow> </msup> <mtext>)</mtext></mrow> </math> Boron atom is smaller than lithium atom but larger than hydrogen atom. The <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> is more stable than <math><mi mathvariant="normal">L</mi><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> but less stable than <math> <mrow> <msub> <mtext>H</mtext> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <mtext>(Bond</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>energy</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>of</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msub> <mtext>B</mtext> <mtext>2</mtext> </msub> <mtext> </mtext><mtext>=</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>290</mtext><mtext> </mtext><mtext>kJ</mtext><mtext> </mtext><msup> <mrow> <mtext>mol</mtext></mrow> <mrow> <mtext>-1</mtext></mrow> </msup> <mtext>)</mtext></mrow> </math>
